title: Deep Learning-Based Fault Identification in Condition Monitoring
summary: This paper presents a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based approach for real-time fault identification in rolling element bearings. The authors analyze the interplay between fault identification accuracy and processing time, and propose a CNN model with various image encodings techniques for quick and accurate fault identification. The results show that the proposed CNN model achieves high accuracy and low processing time, making it suitable for real-time fault identification in condition monitoring.
keywords: ["Deep Learning", "Condition Monitoring", "Fault Identification", "Convolutional Neural Network", "Image Encoding", "Real-time Fault Detection"]

title: Autoencoder-based Condition Monitoring and Anomaly Detection Method for Rotating Machines
summary: This paper proposes an autoencoder-based method for condition monitoring and anomaly detection in rotating machines. The method learns the characteristics of a rotating machine using normal vibration signals and models the healthy state of the machine. A threshold-based approach is then applied to the reconstruction error of unseen data, enabling the detection of unseen anomalies. The proposed method achieves promising results, with an average F1-score of 99.6% on two real-world datasets.

title: A generic framework for scenario exercises using models applied to water-resource management
summary: This paper proposes a conceptual and operational framework for scenario exercises in water-resource management, focusing on information flows between scientists and stakeholders. The framework addresses the challenges of translating narrative information into quantitative model input and vice-versa, and presents original solutions to overcome these challenges. The authors illustrate the framework using four case studies and highlight its potential for guiding model development, setting up participatory and model-based assessment studies, and developing and analyzing scenarios.

title: A GIS tool for modeling anthropogenic noise propagation in natural ecosystems
summary: This paper introduces SPreAD-GIS, a free, open-source GIS application for modeling anthropogenic noise propagation in natural ecosystems. It automates the manual calculations of the SPreAD model to predict the propagation of sound from one or multiple point sources continuously throughout an area of interest. The tool incorporates commonly available datasets on land cover, topography, and weather conditions to calculate noise propagation patterns and excess noise above ambient conditions for one-third octave frequency bands around one or multiple sound sources.

title: A dynamic model for optimally phasing in CO2 capture and storage infrastructure
summary: This paper introduces a new model, SimCCS<sup>TIME</sup> , to optimize the deployment of CO2 capture and storage infrastructure across multiple time periods. The model is designed to be flexible in terms of how much CO2 is captured, transported, and stored in each time period, and considers inter-period tradeoffs and financing and discounting assumptions. The model is an extension of previous SimCCS models and is capable of addressing a range of policy questions related to CCS infrastructure deployment, including the most cost-effective strategy for phasing in a CCS system, the best way to coordinate capacities, and the impact of time on tradeoffs between building high-capacity pipelines and smaller pipelines with more direct routing.
keywords: ["CO2 capture and storage", "Infrastructure modeling", "Spatiotemporal optimization", "Pipeline modeling", "Climate-change policy", "SimCCS"]
